# Implementation Plan: MVP DITA Editor

**Branch**: `001-mvp-dita-editor` | **Date**: 2025-10-23 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/home/kquinn/dita-wysiwyg/specs/001-mvp-dita-editor/spec.md`

**Note**: This file is generated by the `/speckit.plan` command.

## Summary

Build an MVP DITA Editor supporting both Topic editing (WYSIWYG) and DITAMAP management (tree interface). The editor enables technical writers to create topics with paragraphs and lists, validate DITA structure in real-time, and organize topics into hierarchical navigation maps. The technical approach uses React + TypeScript for type safety (CQ2), ProseMirror for WYSIWYG editing with structural validation (UX1), and Zustand for immutable state management (CQ1). Separate models for Topics and Maps enforce architectural decoupling (CQ4).

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.x, ES2022 target
**Primary Dependencies**:
- React 18.x (UI framework)
- ProseMirror (WYSIWYG editor with schema-based validation)
- Zustand (lightweight immutable state management)
- Vite 5.x (build tool and dev server)
- Vitest + React Testing Library (testing framework)

**Storage**: Local file system (Browser File System Access API for save/load in MVP)
**Testing**: Vitest for unit/integration tests, React Testing Library for component tests
**Target Platform**: Fedora Linux, latest stable Firefox and Chrome (PR4)
**Project Type**: Web application (SPA - single page application)
**Performance Goals**:
- Initial render: <1,500ms for 5,000-word topics (PR1)
- Typing latency: <100ms for documents up to 10,000 words (PR2)
- Undo/redo: <500ms (PR3)
- Map tree updates: <200ms for structural changes (UX4)
- Command state updates: <50ms after cursor movement (UX1)

**Constraints**:
- Must enforce DITA 1.3 schema rules for <topic>, <title>, <p>, <ul>, <li>, <map>, <topicref>
- Must prevent all invalid DITA structures (orphaned list items, missing titles)
- Must maintain separate, decoupled Topic and Map state (CQ4)
- Must use immutable data structures for all state mutations (CQ1)
- Offline-capable (no server required for MVP)

**Scale/Scope**:
- Topics: up to 10,000 words
- Maps: up to 100 topic references
- Single user (no collaboration in MVP)
- Limited DITA element set (no tables, images, specializations in MVP)

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

### Code Quality & Maintainability

**CQ1: Data Purity and Immutability** ✅ COMPLIANT
- Using Zustand with immer middleware for immutable state updates
- ProseMirror's transform-based editing inherently immutable
- All Topic and Map state mutations return new state objects

**CQ2: Strong Typing and Validation** ✅ COMPLIANT
- TypeScript 5.x with strict mode enabled
- TypeScript interfaces derived from DITA 1.3 XSD for all elements
- ProseMirror schema strictly types all node and mark definitions
- No `any` types in core logic (enforced via tsconfig strict flags)

**CQ3: Modular Separation of Concerns** ✅ COMPLIANT
- React components observe state via hooks (unidirectional data flow)
- ProseMirror view layer dispatches transactions to state
- State management layer (Zustand stores) separated from UI components
- Clear Model → View → Action → Model architecture

**CQ4: Separate Map and Topic Models** ✅ COMPLIANT
- Dedicated Zustand store for Topic state (`useTopicStore`)
- Dedicated Zustand store for Map state (`useMapStore`)
- No cross-dependencies between stores
- Separate ProseMirror schemas for Topic and Map documents

### Testing Standards

**TS1: Schema Conformance Testing** ✅ PLANNED
- Unit tests for every Topic editing operation (paragraph creation, list conversion)
- Unit tests for every Map operation (add topicref, drag-drop)
- Integration tests validating DITA 1.3 XSD compliance using xml-schema validator
- Fixture-based tests for complex scenarios (nested lists, multi-level maps)

**TS2: View Integrity Testing** ✅ PLANNED
- Jest snapshot tests for all React components
- ProseMirror serialization tests (DOM → DITA XML → DOM roundtrip)
- Visual regression baseline for paragraph, list, and map tree rendering

**TS3: Error and Boundary Condition Testing** ✅ PLANNED
- Tests for invalid operations (orphaned <li>, deleting mandatory <title>)
- Tests for drag-drop edge cases (dropping node onto itself, circular references)
- Tests for undo/redo across valid/invalid state boundaries

### User Experience Consistency

**UX1: Structural Validity Feedback** ✅ COMPLIANT
- ProseMirror command system provides `canExecute` checks
- Toolbar buttons enable/disable based on cursor context via `useEditorState` hook
- Command state updates triggered by ProseMirror selection changes (<50ms)

**UX2: Consistent Visual Mapping** ✅ COMPLIANT
- Single CSS stylesheet for both editor and preview rendering
- ProseMirror DOM output mirrors DITA HTML transformation rules
- Shared style definitions ensure WYSIWYG accuracy

**UX3: Atomicity of Interactions** ✅ COMPLIANT
- "Convert to List" command creates atomic <ul> + <li> structure in single transaction
- "Add Topicref" command creates complete node with all required attributes
- ProseMirror transactions ensure all-or-nothing state changes

**UX4: DITAMAP Tree Interface** ✅ COMPLIANT
- Dedicated `<MapTreeView>` component using react-arborist or similar tree library
- Drag-and-drop via HTML5 Drag API
- Tree re-renders optimized via React.memo and virtualization
- Target <200ms measured via React Profiler

### Performance Requirements

**PR1: Rendering Threshold** ✅ COMPLIANT
- React.memo for all major components
- ProseMirror uses efficient incremental DOM updates
- Lazy loading for large documents via code splitting

**PR2: Input Responsiveness** ✅ COMPLIANT
- ProseMirror's contenteditable-based input is inherently fast
- Validation throttled to avoid blocking typing
- State updates batched via React 18 concurrent rendering

**PR3: Undo/Redo Speed** ✅ COMPLIANT
- ProseMirror history plugin uses minimal diff-based history
- Zustand stores maintain shallow change history
- No full document cloning on each edit

**PR4: Target Platform Baseline** ✅ COMPLIANT
- Vite build targets modern ES2022 (supported by latest Firefox/Chrome)
- Testing configured to run on Fedora Linux via CI
- Browser compatibility verified on Firefox ESR and Chrome stable

### Gate Evaluation

**STATUS: ✅ ALL GATES PASSED**

No constitutional violations. All principles are satisfied by the chosen architecture:
- TypeScript + React + ProseMirror enforces CQ1-CQ3
- Dual Zustand stores enforce CQ4
- Comprehensive test strategy satisfies TS1-TS3
- ProseMirror command system + React optimizations satisfy UX1-UX4 and PR1-PR4

**Structure Decision**: Selected **Web application (SPA)** structure because this is a browser-based single-page application. The structure separates concerns by domain (editor, stores, components, models) rather than by layer, enabling easier feature development. The `src/stores/` directory contains separate Zustand stores for Topic and Map state to enforce CQ4 (model decoupling). The `src/editor/` directory encapsulates all ProseMirror-specific logic, isolating the editing framework from the rest of the application (CQ3).
